newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon expects five pct economic growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon expects five pct economic growth in 1997.

text.p: Lebanon's minister of state for financial affairs said he expects the country's economic growth rate will reach about five percent in 1997, the official National News Agency (NNA) said late on Tuesday.

"We expect that the forecast growth rate during this year will not be below five percent and we hope that in the second half of this year that the real growth rate will exceed five percent," NNA quoted Fouad Siniora as telling parliament.

Lebanon's economic growth rate slipped to four percent in 1996 from 6.5 percent in 1995, well below the 10 percent growth rate projected in the government's postwar reconstruction programme, according to Fransabank, a leading bank.
Siniora said that 100,000 new jobs had been created in the private sector in the past three years.
